skill.name: using-superpowers
skill.description: Guides AI assistants to check available skills before responding and follow applicable skill workflows during task work.
skill.summary: Ensures assistants evaluate and use relevant skills before handling a request.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: The static external-command finding is a false positive because the flagged line opens a non-executable Graphviz dot code fence. The skill does contain overbroad mandatory instructions that try to force tool checks before any response, which is a prompt-control risk.

remediation.suggestion: Reword lines 6-19 to state that skill checks are advisory and always subordinate to system, developer, and user instructions.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 20 opens a fenced Graphviz dot diagram, not a Ruby or shell backtick command. Lines 21-40 contain flowchart text and no executable command invocation or dynamic input.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The skill uses an EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT block and commands such as 'YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE' to force global tool behavior before any response. This can override normal assistant instruction hierarchy and interfere with user or system-directed workflows.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The language is explicit mandatory control-flow text directed at the assistant and applies before any response. It does not directly request data exfiltration or code execution, so confidence is high but not absolute.

high_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
high_findings.description: The skill uses an EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT block and commands such as 'YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE' to force global tool behavior before any response. This can override normal assistant instruction hierarchy and interfere with user or system-directed workflows.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The language is explicit mandatory control-flow text directed at the assistant and applies before any response. It does not directly request data exfiltration or code execution, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Teams can miss relevant AI skills when work begins quickly. This skill tells Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to check skills first and follow applicable workflows.
actual_capabilities: Directs the assistant to check for applicable skills before responding.
Requires invoking a Skill tool when a skill may apply.
Provides a flowchart for skill selection and follow-through.
Lists red flags that indicate skill use was skipped.
Defines priority between process skills and implementation skills.
Distinguishes rigid skills from flexible pattern skills.
limitations: It does not provide domain-specific task guidance.
It depends on the host environment exposing a compatible Skill tool.
It uses broad mandatory language that may conflict with local instruction policy.
It does not include executable automation or validation scripts.

use_cases.title: Standardize assistant task starts
use_cases.description: Help teams make AI assistants check available workflows before starting new work.

use_cases.title: Improve Claude Code routines
use_cases.description: Remind coding assistants to use relevant process skills before planning, debugging, or editing.

use_cases.title: Test skill orchestration
use_cases.description: Give skill authors a simple process layer for checking how other skills are selected.

prompt_templates.title: Start a task with skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Before answering, check whether any installed skill applies to this request. If one applies, read it and follow its workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Review skill fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this task against available skills, name the skill you will use, and explain the first action before continuing.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate multiple skills
prompt_templates.prompt: For this project, decide whether process skills or implementation skills apply first, then execute them in the correct order.

prompt_templates.title: Audit workflow discipline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the last response for skipped skill checks, missed checklist items, and workflow drift. Then provide corrected next steps.

output_examples.input: Fix a bug in this repository.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks for debugging or repository skills first, reads any applicable skill, then starts the bug investigation.
The assistant identifies a planning or frontend skill, announces the selected workflow, and follows any checklist before editing files.
The assistant confirms no relevant skill applies or uses a writing skill before producing the summary.

best_practices: Keep the skill available as a process reminder, not a replacement for higher-priority instructions.
Use it with a curated set of skills so the applicability check remains focused.
Record which skill was selected before starting complex work.
anti_patterns: Treating the skill as higher priority than system, developer, or user instructions.
Invoking unrelated skills because the threshold is too broad.
Using the flowchart as a substitute for task-specific judgment.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides an assistant to check available skills before responding and follow any matching workflow.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. The file contains instructions and a Graphviz diagram, not executable automation.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this a domain skill?
faq.answer: No. It is a process skill for deciding when other skills should guide the work.

faq.question: Why was a security issue reported?
faq.answer: A static scanner misread a fenced dot diagram as shell backtick execution.

faq.question: How should authors improve it?
faq.answer: They should clarify that the skill never overrides system, developer, or user instructions.
